newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy approves Telecom sale decree -Prodi.
newsitem.headline: Italy approves Telecom sale decree -Prodi.

text.p: The Italian cabinet on Friday approved a decree setting out guidelines to privatise state telecoms company Telecom Italia, the new group to be born out of a merger between Telecom and Stet, Prime Minister Romano Prodi said.
He told a news conference the prime ministerial decree would now go to parliament's lower house.

The state telecoms group is due to be privatised by mid-October after holding company Stet's merger with Telecom Italia is complete. The company created by the merger will keep the name of Telecom Italia and is due to become operational on July 18.

"The outline of the prime ministerial decree for the procedures for Telecom Italia's privatisation has been examined and will now pass to the Chamber of Deputies for its opinion," Prodi said after the cabinet meeting had approved his decree.

Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said earlier this week he had aimed in coming days to present the cabinet with a decree on the privatisation which he said could take place in the middle of October.
The upper house Senate last month approved a bill to create a regulatory authority for the telecoms industry which has now to go to the lower house for a final reading.
The Treasury has said that savings shares in Stet and Telecom Italia would not be converted into ordinary shares, a move which has caused anger among international fund managers.

Many investors both in Italy and overseas had bought savings shares, which pay a higher dividend than ordinary stock, in both companies in anticipation they would be able to profit by converting them into voting shares.
At 1255 GMT, Telecom Italia shares were up 2.76 percent at 4,955 lire on a firmer Milan bourse. Stet was 2.58 percent higher at 9,080 lire.
